lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Marta, it's Pierre from the coaching program. Is now still a good time?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How are you doing, really?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hanging in there.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Tell me how the walking went this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I did it 2 days, then the weekend happened.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the walking going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You think you can do it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Walking hurts my knees, so why bother.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can you do it in the morning instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. I don't feel safe walking around here.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. It's been so hot, by 9 in the morning you can't be outside.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. My back was hurting so I didn't push it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You already did the hardest part, which is starting.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: This heat is killing me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Three 10-minute walks count the same as one 30-minute walk.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm too tired for this right now.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I've tried this before and it never lasts.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people walk inside the mall early, before the stores open. It's cool and it's flat.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you use the step counter?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. This heat is killing me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe walk 30 minutes on 3 days?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If the heat gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If it rains I'll walk in the hallway of my building.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Marta. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

Feels unsafe walking locally; not explored

Directive, pushes priority over her ambivalence

flags.reason: Fear-based warning about health without asking permission; drives defensiveness.
Participant says she doesn't feel safe walking locally; coach moved on without exploring.
Directive 'You have to make this a priority' right after her change talk on mental health; undermines autonomy.
Knee pain concern was not explored; coach jumped to morning walks.

score.summary: Marta reported partial walking, named blood sugar and mental health as reasons, and set a realistic goal with a backup plan. The coach repeatedly persuaded or pushed advice (lines 12 and 31), and missed her unsafe-neighborhood and knee-pain concerns.
strengths: Line 8: asked about her personal reason for change, eliciting her blood sugar and mental health motivations.
Line 41: asked for a backup plan for heat, supporting her self-efficacy.
Line 45: affirmed her effort warmly at close.
coaching_tips: Line 12 and line 31: replace warnings and 'have to' with a question, e.g., 'What worries you most about your health right now?'
Line 17: explore 'I don't feel safe walking around here' before offering alternatives; ask what would make her feel safe.
Line 15: reflect the knee pain and ask what she has tried before suggesting other options.
Line 30: reflect her mental-health motivation as change talk instead of pushing priority.
